jurisdiction.name: Romania
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Romania's AI policy rests on the National AI Strategy 2024-2027, approved by Government Decision 832/2024. A 2026 government memorandum names the communications regulator ANCOM as AI Act market surveillance authority and single point of contact, with the financial supervisors, the data protection authority and the digitalisation authority (ADR) covering their fields, but the law implementing the EU AI Act is still being drafted. Three bills on AI and deepfakes are pending in parliament, and the GDPR implementing law sets conditions for automated decisions using sensitive data.
lead_institutions: Authority for the Digitalization of Romania (ADR)
Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digitalization
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. Several government and legislation websites could not be reached, so the AI Act implementing law, pending AI bills and some government orders are listed as leads.

instruments.official_title: Strategia națională în domeniul inteligenței artificiale 2024-2027
instruments.english_title: National Strategy in the Field of Artificial Intelligence 2024-2027
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of Romania (approved by Government Decision no. 832/2024; prepared by the Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digitalisation and the Authority for the Digitalization of Romania)
instruments.current_status: Annex no. 1 to Government Decision (HG) no. 832/2024, listed on the legislation portal as published in Monitorul Oficial no. 730 of 25 July 2024. The strategy covers 2024-2027 and is the strategy in force; no later amendment was found.
instruments.summary: Romania's first national AI strategy (SN-IA) for 2024-2027, with six general objectives: AI education and skills, infrastructure and datasets, the national AI research-development-innovation system, technology transfer through partnerships, AI adoption across society (including government and the public sector), and an AI governance and regulatory system. It sets programmes and measures with responsible institutions, indicators and funding sources, and proposes to examine structures such as a national AI regulatory authority under the EU AI Act, an AI coordination office in ministries, a trustworthy-AI centre, AI regulatory sandboxes and a support centre for data, algorithms and AI in public administration. Implementation is coordinated by an Interministerial Commission chaired by the minister of research, innovation and digitalisation, which was to adopt its rules, work plan and monitoring methodology within 60 days of approval.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy and the framework for Romania's AI governance architecture.

It was the expert proposal from which the National AI Strategy 2024-2027 (HG 832/2024) was developed; superseded by that strategy.
instruments.summary: Expert proposal for a national AI strategic framework for 2023-2027, prepared under the EU-funded SIPOCA 704 project led by the Authority for the Digitalization of Romania with the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca. It sets out the vision, principles, context analysis and general objectives (skills, infrastructure and data, research, technology transfer, adoption in society and the public sector, governance and regulation) later carried into the adopted 2024-2027 strategy. It had no legal effect and served as the basis for the government strategy.

instruments.summary: Romania's GDPR implementing law. Article 3(1) allows processing of genetic, biometric or health data for automated decision-making or profiling only with the data subject's explicit consent or under express legal provisions with appropriate safeguards; other articles regulate national identification numbers, employee monitoring, journalistic and research processing, data protection officers, certification bodies and corrective measures and fines for public authorities. ANSPDCP supervises its application.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National data protection law; sets a specific condition for automated decision-making and profiling with sensitive data.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Romania's legislation sources, the Senate bill database, the government, ministries and regulators were searched. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for risk and assurance, procurement, cybersecurity, transparency, standards, readiness indices, generative AI or international agreements. The legislation portal and the digital ministry, government secretariat, Chamber of Deputies and cyber agency sites were unavailable, so the text of the government decision approving the AI strategy, the order setting up the Romanian AI Committee and a deepfake guide are listed as leads to check later.
coverage_audit.technical_note: Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. legislatie.just.ro HTTP/2 error/502, mcid.gov.ro incomplete TLS chain/503, sgg.gov.ro reset/503, cdep.ro reset, dnsc.ro 403. Strategy annex read from ADR's link; HG 832/2024 decision text not read. Dropped i-ba085cd54a95 (SIPOCA 704 project page, not an instrument). Memorandum dated by year only. Convention 108: Law 682/2001, recorded on the COE file. Units covered: Law: Legislation portal (legislatie.just.ro) unreachable (protocol errors / HTTP 502); used ANSPDCP legislation page (Law 190/2018 recorded) and the Senate legislative database (three AI/deepfake bills, all pending in the Chamber, held as leads). No adopted AI-specific law and no adopted AI Act implementing law found; cdep.ro unreachable (connection reset).; Government: National AI Strategy 2024-2027 (HG 832/2024 annex) re-checked and retitled; 2023 strategic framework proposal added (historical); 2026 Government Memorandum on AI Act authorities added; ADR project record flagged. mcid.gov.ro (incomplete TLS chain; WebFetch 503) and sgg.gov.ro (connection reset; WebFetch 503) unreachable, so the HG text and the Order establishing the Romanian AI Committee are leads. No public-sector GenAI guideline found.; Ministries: Searched education (AI guide still a draft, lead), defence, health, justice, finance/ANAF, interior via site search: no published AI policy documents found.; Regulators: ANCOM: AI information section and the Memorandum (recorded via ANCOM); ANSPDCP: no national AI guidance or AI decision found (only EDPB/WP29 translations); ASF: only a Romanian translation of an ESMA investor factsheet on AI (regional, not recorded); BNR: no AI guidance (reports only); DNSC: deepfake guide reported but dnsc.ro returns 403 (lead).. Not reached: legislatie.just.ro (HG 832/2024 decision text, Order 20484/2023); mcid.gov.ro (strategy page, Committee order); sgg.gov.ro (HG 832/2024 PDF); cdep.ro bill dossiers; dnsc.ro. Could not verify: HG 832/2024 decision text, its date (11 July 2024) and gazette (MO 730/25 July 2024): legislatie.just.ro and sgg.gov.ro unreachable via curl and WebFetch; publication_date 2024-07-25 kept from the existing record.; Law 190/2018 gazette issue and effective date (not printed on the ANSPDCP copy).; Order MCID 20484/2023 (Romanian AI Committee) - official text unreachable (lead).; DNSC deepfake guide - dnsc.ro 403 (lead).. risk-assurance, procurement, cyber-security, transparency, standards, index-readiness, generative-ai, international: no material found.
